chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: Muldaur's idea for the Ellington-Kay Davis style 'Transblucency'
summary: Carter told Collins the wordless voice-and-horn number was Muldaur's idea, and Willard says Kay Davis was surprised to be remembered.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: That album you did, is that Wafers in

I think so, yes, yes. But you know, she's a very astute young lady. I -- we did one thing, one tune we did, transbluency. Now, this was done by Duke and Kay Davis. No lyrics, just voice and horns. So I -- it came off so well, Maria -- Marie -- Benny Carter was playing the horn, you know, so it was just like a duet. And I -- and of course Benny arranged it for her. And I said, Benny, that was a marvelous idea you had for Maria Muldaur. He said, no, John, she heard this record and had the idea and approached me about it.
She heard Kay and Duke's record?

She heard the record and she approached -- Benny, she said, I'd like to do that, he said I can't take credit for that. You know, despite the fact that it came off so beautifully he said it was her idea, not mine. And she did quite a few of Duke's things and some of Billie Holiday's things. But she lives in Woodstock so you know where her roots are. She's really -- how would you say, a folk singer? From that school, any way. You know. But she's -- I think she's going places in the contemporary you know, in the jazz world I think that she'll make it. Very good.
I've read several reviews of hers, and they made reference to Kay's record, and I told Kay when
--and she said I didn't think anybody remembered me any more.
Oh, boy, how can they forget her. Yeah, but any way it was Maria's idea, it was not Benny's. So I wasn't aware of that. But a very successful tour.
